title: "The tables"
include-after-body: _search.html

```{r}
#| label: load
library(data.table)
# Everything on this page comes from the metadata pipeline's outputs
# (metadata/run_pipeline.sh) plus the validator report. Only samplingProtocol
# and temporalCoverage are still read from __dataset.json, as prose.
tags <- as.data.table(read.csv("../metadata/tags.csv", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
bib  <- as.data.table(read.csv("../metadata/biblio.csv", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
num  <- as.data.table(read.csv("../metadata/metadata.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
val  <- as.data.table(read.csv("../validate/report.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
prose <- rbindlist(lapply(list.files("../output", "__dataset.json$", full.names = TRUE), function(f) {
  j <- jsonlite::read_json(f)
  data.table(table = j$table, protocol = j$samplingProtocol, coverage = j$temporalCoverage)
}))
d <- merge(tags, bib[, .(table, title, description, citation, licence = spdx, sourceURL = source_url)], by = "table")
d <- merge(d, num[, .(table, n_units, n_taxa, n_periods, n_occasions, n_rows, sample_floor,
                      columns = gsub("|", ", ", variables, fixed = TRUE), coarsened = coordinates_coarsened,
                      survey_evidence, script)], by = "table")
d <- merge(d, prose, by = "table")
d <- merge(d, val[, .(table, irw_v1, irw_warnings)], by = "table")
dn <- as.data.table(read.csv("../releases/data_notes.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = "character"))
setorder(d, table)
redivis <- "https://redivis.com/datasets/4j5q"
gh <- "https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/blob/main"
```

Every table below was built by a script in the repository's `data/`
directory from a public deposit, validated against the draft standard, and published on Redivis as the dataset
[`datapages.eco`](`r redivis`). Each table ships with a `__taxa`
side table (taxon resolution via GBIF, plus traits where the source has them),
a `__periods` side table where there are primary periods, `__units` or
`__traps` where the sampling frame or trap layout needs one, and a
`__dataset.json` with the EML and Darwin Core fields the standard borrows.
Tables whose notes begin "Experimental" use the standard's experimental
semantics (E9) and may be restructured between versions; "Declared stretch"
marks a design where `occasion` indexes a category rather than a replicate in
time.

The **Floor** column is the standard's sample floor, 30 or more units and 2
or more occasions (or periods). It is a filter, not an admission rule: tables
below it are published like any other and say so, and a user who needs the
floor excludes them on `sample_floor` in the tags.

## Summary

`r nrow(d)` tables. Start typing to search across names, model families, taxa,
protocols and licences; each name links to the table's full entry below.

```{=html}
<input type="text" id="tableSearch" placeholder="Search tables..." oninput="filterRows('tableSearch', 'summary-table', 'table-count', 'table')" class="eco-search">
<p id="table-count" class="eco-search-count"></p>
```

::: {#summary-table .eco-searchable}

```{r}
#| label: summary
#| output: asis
d[, dims := sprintf("%s × %s × %s × %s", n_units, n_taxa, n_periods, n_occasions)]
d[, floor := ifelse(sample_floor == "meets", "meets", "below")]
d[, name := sprintf("[`%s`](#%s)", table, table)]
out <- d[, .(Table = name, Family = model_family, Taxa = taxon_group,
             Protocol = sampling_protocol, `Units × taxa × periods × occasions` = dims,
             Rows = format(n_rows, big.mark = ","), Licence = licence, Floor = floor)]
cat(knitr::kable(out, format = "pipe"), sep = "\n")
```

:::

The four dimensions are counts of distinct `unit`, `taxon`, `period` and
`occasion` values. The row count is the number of survey observations, which
is smaller than the product of the four whenever some unit-occasion
combinations were not surveyed.

## Each table

```{r}
#| label: cards
#| output: asis
for (i in seq_len(nrow(d))) {
  r <- d[i]
  cat(sprintf("\n### `%s` {#%s}\n\n", r$table, r$table))
  cat(sprintf("**%s**\n\n", r$title))
  cat(sprintf("%s\n\n", r$description))
  cat("| | |\n|---|---|\n")
  cat(sprintf("| Family | %s |\n", r$model_family))
  cat(sprintf("| Design | %s |\n", r$design))
  cat(sprintf("| Protocol | %s |\n", r$protocol))
  cat(sprintf("| Response | `%s` |\n", r$response_type))
  cat(sprintf("| Coverage | %s; %s; %s |\n", r$country, r$realm, r$coverage))
  cat(sprintf("| Coordinates | %s |\n", r$coordinates))
  cat(sprintf("| Size | %s units, %s taxa, %s periods, %s occasions, %s rows |\n",
              r$n_units, r$n_taxa, r$n_periods, r$n_occasions, format(r$n_rows, big.mark = ",")))
  cat(sprintf("| Sample floor | %s |\n", r$sample_floor))
  cat(sprintf("| Survey evidence | `%s` |\n", r$survey_evidence))
  cat(sprintf("| Columns | %s |\n", paste0("`", strsplit(r$columns, ", ")[[1]], "`", collapse = " ")))
  cat(sprintf("| Source | [%s](%s), %s |\n", r$sourceURL, r$sourceURL, r$licence))
  cat(sprintf("| Script | [`%s`](%s/%s) |\n", r$script, gh, r$script))
  if (nzchar(r$notes)) cat(sprintf("\nNotes: %s\n", r$notes))
  for (nn in dn[table == r$table]$note) cat(sprintf("\n**Data note.** %s\n", nn))
  # a dataset and its paper share one citation field; show each on its own line
  cat(sprintf("\nCitation: %s\n", gsub("\\. (Paper|Data): ", ".\n\n\\1: ", r$citation)))
}
```

## Getting the data

The dataset is on Redivis as [`datapages.eco`](`r redivis`). Its public
access level is "data", so every table is served as CSV to anyone, no account
needed; the [R package](r.html) reads it that way:

```r
remotes::install_github("ben-domingue/eco", subdir = "Rpkg")
library(eco)
eco_filter(model_family = "Single-season occupancy") |> head(1) |>
  eco_fetch() |> eco_to_unmarked() |> unmarked::occu(~1 ~1, data = _)
```

The standard is still a draft, so names and columns may change between
versions; released versions do not. Every table is rebuilt from its source
deposit by its script in the repository's `data/` directory:

```sh
Rscript data/<table>.R
```

from the repository root. The scripts cache downloads and are deterministic,
with assertions on facts about each source so that a changed deposit fails
loudly.
